summary.one_liner: A curated checklist of technical due diligence questions that a company can answer to get a snapshot of its technology state for valuation and investment purposes.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a question list rather than a software project. It is organized into sections: Business, Product/Service, Team/Hiring/Human resources, Technology/Code, Architecture and Infrastructure, Security/Continuity/Monitoring, and Budgeting. Each section contains open-ended questions covering topics such as compliance with GDPR/KVKK, roadmap planning, hiring and onboarding, code review and testing practices, release and deployment processes, vendor dependence, scaling, backups, DDoS exposure, and disaster recovery. The intro says the goal is for a company to answer the questions honestly to gain a clearer view of its own state. The author offers a paid follow-up evaluation report and auditing services. The list contains no code or tooling.
use_cases: preparing for investor technical due diligence
reviewing a company's technology team and processes before funding
generating questions for a technical audit
checking vendor dependence and disaster recovery readiness
notable: Covers business, product, team, code, infrastructure, security, and budget in one checklist
Questions on human resources, hiring, and team dynamics alongside technical topics
Includes compliance questions for GDPR and KVKK
Asks about bus factor, single points of failure, and dependency risk
Intended for self-assessment before fundraising or investment rounds
caveats: Not software; it provides questions only, with no tooling or automated checks
The author offers paid follow-up evaluation and auditing services
